title.zh: 卷四十 志第十六 地理一
title.raw: 卷四十 志第十六 地理一 Volume 40 Treatises 16: Geography 1

translations.literal: Treatise Sixteen, Geography One.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Sixteen: Geography, Part One.

sentences.zh: 自黃帝畫野置監，唐、虞分州建牧，沿及三代，下逮宋、元，廢興因革此類推，萬物無所差別，「天與地卑，山與澤平」。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor, who mapped the wilds and set overseers, through Tang and Yu, who divided provinces and appointed herdsmen, down through the Three Dynasties to Song and Yuan—abolition and establishment, succession and reform may be inferred by this pattern; among the ten thousand things nothing differs: "Heaven is level with earth; mountains are level with marshes."
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor mapping the realm and appointing overseers, through Tang and Yu dividing domains and installing regional lords, and on through the Three Dynasties down to Song and Yuan, rise and fall follow the same logic—nothing in the world is truly apart. As the saying has it: "Heaven stands no higher than earth; mountains stand no higher than marshes."

translations.literal: As for its doctrines, with [,] the previous histories are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Those doctrines, and the fuller accounts in earlier histories, are already on record.

sentences.zh: 明太祖奮起淮右，首定金陵，西克湖、湘，東兼吳、會，然後遣將北伐，並山東，收河南，進取幽、燕，分軍四出，芟除秦、晉，訖於嶺表。

translations.literal: The Ming founding emperor rose on the Huai right, first secured Jinling, westward conquered Hu and Xiang, eastward combined Wu and Kuai, then sent generals on a northern campaign, together took Shandong, received Henan, advanced to take You and Yan, divided armies on four sides, mowed down Qin and Jin, reaching to Lingbiao.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming founder rose in the Huai River region, first took Jinling, then conquered Hunan and Hubei in the west and Wu and Zhejiang in the east, sent armies north to seize Shandong and Henan, pushed into Hebei and Beijing, fanned out on four fronts to subdue Shaanxi and Shanxi, and reached the far south.

sentences.zh: 最後削平巴、蜀，收復滇南。

translations.literal: At last leveled Ba and Shu, recovered southern Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He finally pacified Sichuan and recovered southern Yunnan.

translations.literal: Where Yu's footprints covered, all entered the territory map.
translations.idiomatic: Every region within Yu the Great's traditional domain was brought into the imperial map.

translations.literal: Since recent antiquity, what had never been.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing like it had been seen in recent antiquity.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，建都江表，革元中書省，以京畿應天諸府直隸京師。

translations.literal: Early Hongwu, capital established on the Jiang tables, abolished Yuan Central Secretariat, made the Yingtian-region prefectures directly attached to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongwu the court set the capital on the lower Yangtze, abolished the Yuan Central Secretariat, and placed the Yingtian prefectures under direct capital jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 後乃盡革行中書省，置十三布政使司，分領天下府州縣及羈縻諸司。

translations.literal: Later then abolished all provincial commissions, established thirteen provincial administration commissions, separately overseeing all under heaven's prefectures, departments, counties, and suzerain-submissive commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Later it abolished every provincial commission and created thirteen provincial administration commissions to govern the empire's prefectures, departments, counties, and loosely ruled frontier offices.

sentences.zh: 又置十五都指揮使司以領衛所番漢諸軍，其邊境海疆則增置行都指揮使司，而於京師建五軍都督府，俾外都指揮使司各以其方附焉。

translations.literal: Also established fifteen regional military commands to lead guards, posts, and fan and Han armies; on borderlands and sea coasts added regional frontier military commands; at the capital established the Five Armies supreme command, so that outer regional commands each attached by their region.
translations.idiomatic: It also set up fifteen regional military commands over guards, posts, and mixed frontier and Han forces; added frontier regional commands along borders and coasts; and at the capital founded the Five Armies supreme command, to which the outer commands were attached by region.

sentences.zh: 成祖定都北京，北倚羣山，東臨滄海，南面而臨天下，乃以北平爲直隸，又增設貴州、交址二布政使司。

translations.literal: The Yongle emperor fixed the capital at Beijing, north relying on mountain ranges, east facing the blue sea, south-facing overlooking all under heaven; then made Beiping directly attached, and further added Guizhou and Jiaozhi provincial administration commissions.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle emperor moved the capital to Beijing, backed by mountains and facing the sea to the east, ruling the realm from the south-facing throne. He made Beiping a directly attached region and added provincial administration commissions for Guizhou and Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣之際，南交屢叛，旋復棄之外徼。

translations.literal: At the Ren-Xuan period, southern Jiao repeatedly rebelled, soon again abandoned to the outer marches.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongxi and Xuande reigns Jiaozhi rebelled repeatedly and was soon abandoned to the outer frontier.

sentences.zh: 終明之世，爲直隸者二：曰京師，曰南京。

translations.literal: Through the Ming dynasty's age, as directly attached there were two: called the capital, called Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: For the whole Ming period there were two directly attached regions: the capital and Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 爲布政使司者十三：曰山東，曰山西，曰河南，曰陝西，曰四川，曰湖廣，曰浙江，曰江西，曰福建，曰廣東，曰廣西，曰云南，曰貴州。

translations.literal: As provincial administration commissions there were thirteen: called Shandong, called Shanxi, called Henan, called Shaanxi, called Sichuan, called Huguang, called Zhejiang, called Jiangxi, called Fujian, called Guangdong, called Guangxi, called Yunnan, called Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: There were thirteen provincial administration commissions: Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Huguang, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 其分統之府百有四十，州百九十有三，縣千一百三十有八。

translations.literal: Their subordinate prefectures: one hundred forty; departments one hundred ninety-three; counties one thousand one hundred thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Under them stood 140 prefectures, 193 departments, and 1,138 counties.

sentences.zh: 羈縻之府十有九，州四十有七，縣六。

translations.literal: Suzerain-submissive prefectures: nineteen; departments forty-seven; counties six.
translations.idiomatic: In loosely ruled territories there were 19 prefectures, 47 departments, and 6 counties.

sentences.zh: 編裏六萬九千五百五十有六。

translations.literal: Registered li: sixty-nine thousand five hundred fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Registered li totaled 69,556.

sentences.zh: 而兩京都督府分統都指揮使司十有六，行都指揮使司五，曰北平、曰山西、曰陝西、曰四川、曰福建，留守司二。

translations.literal: The two capitals' supreme commands separately oversaw sixteen regional military commands; five regional frontier military commands—called Beiping, called Shanxi, called Shaanxi, called Sichuan, called Fujian; garrison commands two.
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals' supreme commands oversaw sixteen regional military commands and five frontier regional commands—Beiping, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Fujian—plus two garrison commands.

sentences.zh: 所屬衛四百九十有三，所二千五百九十有三，守禦千戶所三百一十有五。

translations.literal: Subordinate guards four hundred ninety-three, posts two thousand five hundred ninety-three, defensive thousand-household posts three hundred fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: Under them were 493 guards, 2,593 posts, and 315 defensive thousand-household posts.

sentences.zh: 又土官宣慰司十有一，宣撫司十，安撫司二十有二，招討司一，長官司一百六十有九，蠻夷長官司五。

translations.literal: Also native-official pacification commissions eleven, consolation commissions ten, soothing commissions twenty-two, punitive-commission one, native chieftain offices one hundred sixty-nine, barbarian chieftain offices five.
translations.idiomatic: Native offices included 11 pacification commissions, 10 consolation commissions, 22 soothing commissions, 1 punitive commission, 169 chieftain offices, and 5 barbarian chieftain offices.

sentences.zh: 其邊陲要地稱重鎮者凡九：曰遼東，曰薊州，曰宣府，曰大同，曰榆林，曰寧夏，曰甘肅，曰太原，曰固原。

translations.literal: Border strategic places counted as weighty garrisons: nine in all—called Liaodong, called Jizhou, called Xuanfu, called Datong, called Yulin, called Ningxia, called Gansu, called Taiyuan, called Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Nine frontier strongholds ranked as major garrisons: Liaodong, Jizhou, Xuanfu, Datong, Yulin, Ningxia, Gansu, Taiyuan, and Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 皆分統衛所關堡，環列兵戎。

translations.literal: All separately oversaw guards, posts, passes, and forts, ring-arranged troops.
translations.idiomatic: Each commanded a ring of guards, posts, passes, and forts with troops stationed around them.

sentences.zh: 綱維佈置，可謂深且固矣。

translations.literal: The guiding net's disposition, may be called deep and solid.
translations.idiomatic: The overall military layout was deep and firm indeed.

sentences.zh: 計明初封略，東起朝鮮，西據吐番，南包安南，北距大磧用，東西一萬一千七百五十里，南北一萬零九百四里。

translations.literal: Calculating early Ming territory: east from Korea, west holding Tufan, south enclosing Annan, north reaching the great desert, east-west eleven thousand seven hundred fifty li, north-south ten thousand ninety-four li.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's height the realm ran from Korea in the east to Tibet in the west, Annan in the south, and the northern deserts—11,750 li east to west and 10,094 li north to south.

sentences.zh: 自成祖棄大寧，徙東勝，宣宗遷開平於獨石，世宗時復棄哈密、河套，則東起遼海，西至嘉峪，南至瓊、崖，北抵雲、朔，東西萬餘里，南北萬里。

translations.literal: From the time Cheng Zu abandoned Da Ning, moved Dong Sheng, the Xuande emperor moved Kaiping to Dushi, the Shizong era again abandoned Hami and the Ordos bend—then east from Liaohai, west to Jiayu Pass, south to Qiong and Ya, north to Yun and Shuo; east-west ten thousand-odd li, north-south ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle gave up Da Ning, shifted Dong Sheng, Xuande moved Kaiping to Dushi, and the Jiajing court again abandoned Hami and the Ordos bend, the frontier ran from Liaodong to Jiayu Pass, Hainan and Yazhou in the south, and Datong-Shuozhou in the north—over ten thousand li each way.

sentences.zh: 其聲教所訖，歲時納贄，而非命吏置籍，侯尉羈屬者，不在此數。

translations.literal: Where civilizing influence reached, yearly tribute offered, yet not ordered officials placed registers, frontier commandants suzerain-attached—are not in this count.
translations.idiomatic: States that accepted Ming ritual and sent annual tribute but were not assigned regular officials, registers, or frontier commandants are not included in these figures.

translations.literal: Alas, how grand!
translations.idiomatic: Truly it was magnificent!

sentences.zh: 論者謂交趾之棄，未爲失圖，而開平近遷，則守衛益薄，雖置萬全都指揮使司，不足以鎮伏山後諸部，故再傳而有土木之變。

translations.literal: Discussants say abandoning Jiaozhi was not losing the plan, but Kaiping's near removal then guard-defense grew thinner; though establishing the Wanquan regional military command, it was insufficient to subdue the mountain-behind tribes—thus two transmissions later came the Tumu crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators hold that giving up Jiaozhi was not a strategic blunder, but moving Kaiping closer in thinned frontier defense; even the Wanquan regional command could not hold down the tribes beyond the mountains, and within two reigns came the Tumu disaster.

sentences.zh: 然睿皇自以失律蒙塵，非由經制未備。

translations.literal: Yet the sagely emperor himself took disorder in discipline, dust on the throne—not because institutions were unready.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the captured emperor blamed his own military failure, not a defective institutional framework.

sentences.zh: 景帝任賢才，修守禦，國步未移，乘輿旋復。

translations.literal: The Jingdi emperor employed worthy talent, repaired defensive posts; the state's step did not shift, the imperial carriage soon returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingtai emperor appointed able men and strengthened defenses; the dynasty did not falter, and the throne was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，三衛者，一隅之隘，而無關大計也審矣。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, the three guards were one corner's narrows, and without relation to the great plan—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, the three guards were a narrow corner of the frontier and scarcely mattered to the larger design.

sentences.zh: 至其季世，流寇首禍於西陲，浸尋蔓延，中原爲之糜爛。

translations.literal: At its late age, roaming bandits first brought disaster on the western marches, gradually spreading; the central plains for this were ground to pulp.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's final years rebel armies first rose on the western frontier and spread until the central plains lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 金湯之固不足以制土崩，皈宇之廣不足以成掎角。

translations.literal: Golden moats' solidity was insufficient to restrain earthen collapse; the returned realm's breadth was insufficient to complete paired-horn strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Fortresses of bronze could not stop the empire from crumbling; vast territory could not be turned into mutual support.

sentences.zh: 疆圉不蹙於曩時，形勝無虧於初盛，而強弱懸殊，興亡異數者，天降喪亂，昏椓內訌，人事之乖，而非地利之失也。

translations.literal: The border did not shrink from former times, strategic advantage did not lose from first flourishing—yet strong and weak hung far apart, rise and fall differed in number: Heaven sent ruin and chaos, muddled rulers and internal strife, human affairs' perversity, and not terrain's loss.
translations.idiomatic: Borders were no narrower than before and terrain no weaker than at the height of power, yet strength and weakness diverged wildly—because Heaven sent chaos, rulers grew corrupt, and factions tore the court apart. The fall was human, not geographical.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「在德不在險」，詎不信夫!今考其升降之差，沿革之故， 具著於篇。

translations.literal: The saying goes: "In virtue, not in terrain"—how can one not believe! Now examining its rise-and-fall differences, succession-and-reform causes, all fully set out in the chapters.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, "Safety lies in virtue, not in walls"—and how true that proved. What follows records every shift in jurisdiction and every change in administration.

translations.literal: Compose "Geography Treatise."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Geography Treatise was written.

translations.literal: ▲ Capital, Nanjing
translations.idiomatic: ▲ The Capital and Nanjing

sentences.zh: 京師《禹貢》冀、兗、豫三州之域，元直隸中書省。

translations.literal: ▲ Capital: "Yu Gong" Ji, Yan, and Yu three provinces' domains; Yuan directly attached Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ The Capital lay in the Ji, Yan, and Yu regions of the Yu Gong; under the Yuan it formed part of the directly governed Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年四月分屬河南、山東兩行中書省。

translations.literal: Hongwu year one, fourth month, divided and attached to Henan and Shandong two provincial commissions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Hongwu 1 it was split between the Henan and Shandong provincial commissions.

sentences.zh: 二年三月置北平等處行中書省，治北平府。

translations.literal: Year two, third month, established Beiping and other places provincial commission, administering Beiping prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 2 a provincial commission for Beiping and adjacent areas was created, seated at Beiping prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先屬山東、河南者皆復其舊。

translations.literal: What first belonged to Shandong and Henan all returned to their old.
translations.idiomatic: Territories previously assigned to Shandong and Henan were restored to their former jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 領府八，州三十七，縣一百三十六。

translations.literal: Governed prefectures eight, departments thirty-seven, counties one hundred thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: It governed eight prefectures, thirty-seven departments, and 136 counties.

translations.literal: Eighth month established Yanshan regional guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Yanshan regional guard was established.

translations.literal: With the provincial commission same administration.
translations.idiomatic: It shared the same seat as the provincial commission.

sentences.zh: 八年十月改都衛爲北平都指揮使司。

translations.literal: Year eight, tenth month, changed regional guard to Beiping regional military command.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 8 the regional guard became the Beiping regional military command.

sentences.zh: 九年六月改行中書省爲承宣布政使司。

translations.literal: Year nine, sixth month, changed provincial commission to Pacification and Notification provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 9 the provincial commission became a provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年正月建北京於順天府，稱爲「行在」。

translations.literal: Yongle year one, first month, established Beijing at Shuntian prefecture, called "traveling residence."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongle 1 Beijing was founded at Shuntian prefecture and styled the "traveling residence."

sentences.zh: 二月罷北平布政使司，以所領直隸北京行部；

translations.literal: Second month abolished Beiping provincial administration commission, its governed directly attached to Beijing traveling ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Beiping provincial administration commission was abolished and its jurisdictions placed under the Beijing traveling ministry.

sentences.zh: 罷北平都指揮使司，以所領直隸北京留守行後軍都督府。

translations.literal: Abolished Beiping regional military command, its governed directly attached to Beijing garrison traveling Rear Army supreme command.
translations.idiomatic: The Beiping regional military command was abolished and its forces placed under the Beijing garrison traveling Rear Army supreme command.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月改北京爲京師。

translations.literal: Year nineteen, first month, changed Beijing to capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 19 Beijing was renamed the capital.

sentences.zh: 罷北京留守行後軍都督府，直隸後軍都督府。

translations.literal: Abolished Beijing garrison traveling Rear Army supreme command, directly attached to Rear Army supreme command.
translations.idiomatic: The Beijing garrison traveling Rear Army supreme command was abolished and its forces placed directly under the Rear Army supreme command.

sentences.zh: 衛所有實土者附見，無實土者不載。

translations.literal: Guards and posts with real territory are attached in the text; those without real territory are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Guards and posts with fixed territory are noted where relevant; those without territory are omitted.

translations.literal: Abolished Beijing traveling ministry, directly attached to the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The Beijing traveling ministry was abolished and the region placed under the Six Ministries.

translations.literal: Early Hongxi, still called traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Hongxi reign it was again called the traveling residence.

sentences.zh: 正統六年十一月罷稱行在，定爲京師。

translations.literal: Zhengtong year six, eleventh month, abolished calling traveling residence, fixed as capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Zhengtong 6 the "traveling residence" title was dropped and the city fixed as the capital.

sentences.zh: 府八，直隸州二，屬州十七，縣一百一十六。

translations.literal: Prefectures eight, directly attached departments two, dependent departments seventeen, counties one hundred sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: It comprised eight prefectures, two directly attached departments, seventeen dependent departments, and 116 counties.

sentences.zh: 爲裏三千二百三十有奇。

translations.literal: As li: three thousand two hundred thirty-odd.
translations.idiomatic: Registered li numbered somewhat more than 3,230.

sentences.zh: 府州縣建置沿革，俱自元始。

translations.literal: Prefecture, department, and county establishment succession-and-reform, all from Yuan beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Changes in prefectures, departments, and counties are traced from the Yuan onward.

sentences.zh: 其沿革年月已見《元史志》者，不載。

translations.literal: Those succession-and-reform years already seen in "Yuan History Treatise" are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Dates already given in the Yuan History are not repeated.

sentences.zh: 其未見《元史志》及明改元舊，並新增、新廢者，悉書。

translations.literal: Those not seen in "Yuan History Treatise" and Ming-era name changes, together with newly added and newly abolished—are all written.
translations.idiomatic: Entries absent from the Yuan History, Ming renaming, and newly created or abolished units are all listed.

translations.literal: North reaching Xuanfu, outside is borderland.
translations.idiomatic: To the north it reached Xuanfu; beyond lay the frontier.

translations.literal: East reaching Liaohai, bordering Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: To the east it reached the Liaodong coast, bordering Shandong.

sentences.zh: 南至東明，與山東、河南界。

translations.literal: South reaching Dongming, bordering Shandong and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: To the south it reached Dongming, bordering Shandong and Henan.

translations.literal: West reaching Fuping, bordering Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: To the west it reached Fuping, bordering Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六，年編戶三十三萬四千七百九十二，口一百九十二萬六千五百九十五。

translations.literal: Hongwu twenty-six, year registered households three hundred thirty-four thousand seven hundred ninety-two, mouths one million nine hundred twenty-six thousand five hundred ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 26 it had 334,792 registered households and 1,926,595 persons.

sentences.zh: 順天府元大都路，直隸中書省。

translations.literal: Shuntian prefecture: Yuan Dadu circuit, directly attached Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian prefecture had been the Yuan Dadu circuit under the directly governed Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年八月改爲北平府。

translations.literal: Hongwu year one, eighth month, changed to Beiping prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Hongwu 1 it became Beiping prefecture.

translations.literal: Tenth month belonged to Shandong provincial commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month it was placed under the Shandong provincial commission.

translations.literal: Year two, third month, changed to belong to Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 2 it was transferred back to Beiping jurisdiction.

translations.literal: Year three, fourth month, established Yan prince mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 3 the mansion of the Prince of Yan was established.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年正月升爲北京，改府爲順天府。

translations.literal: Yongle year one, first month, promoted to Beijing, changed prefecture to Shuntian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongle 1 it was elevated to Beijing and the prefecture renamed Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年閏七月詔建北京宮殿，修城垣。

translations.literal: Yongle year four, intercalary seventh month, edict to build Beijing palace halls, repair city walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month of Yongle 4 an edict ordered construction of the Beijing palaces and repair of the city walls.

translations.literal: Year nineteen, first month, announced completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 19 the work was declared complete.

sentences.zh: 宮城週六里一十六步，亦曰紫禁城。

translations.literal: Palace city perimeter six li sixteen paces, also called Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: The palace city measured six li and sixteen paces in circumference and was also called the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 門八：正南第一重曰承天，第二重曰端門，第三重曰午門，東曰東華，西曰西華，北曰玄武。

translations.literal: Gates eight: due south first layer called Chengtian, second layer called Duan, third layer called Wu; east called Donghua, west called Xihua, north called Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: It had eight gates: on the south, from outside in, Chengtian, Duan, and Wu; on the east Donghua; on the west Xihua; on the north Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 宮城之外爲皇城，週一十八里有奇。

translations.literal: Outside the palace city was the imperial city, perimeter eighteen-odd li.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the palace city lay the imperial city, somewhat more than eighteen li around.

sentences.zh: 門六：正南曰大明，東曰東安，西曰西安，北曰北安，大明門東轉曰長安左，西轉曰長安右。

translations.literal: Gates six: due south called Daming; east called Dong'an; west called Xi'an; north called Bei'an; east of Daming Gate turning called Chang'an Left; west turning called Chang'an Right.
translations.idiomatic: It had six gates: Daming on the south; Dong'an on the east; Xi'an on the west; Bei'an on the north; and, branching from Daming Gate, Chang'an Left to the east and Chang'an Right to the west.

sentences.zh: 皇城之外曰京城，週四十五里。

translations.literal: Outside the imperial city was called the capital city, perimeter forty-five li.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the imperial city stood the outer capital, forty-five li in circuit.

sentences.zh: 門九：正南曰麗正，正統初改曰正陽；

translations.literal: Gates nine: due south called Lizheng; early Zhengtong changed to Zhengyang;
translations.idiomatic: It had nine gates: on the south, Lizheng—renamed Zhengyang early in Zhengtong;

sentences.zh: 南之左曰文明，後曰崇文；

translations.literal: south's left called Wenming, later called Chongwen;
translations.idiomatic: to the south-left, Wenming, later Chongwen;

sentences.zh: 南之右曰順城，後曰宣武；

translations.literal: south's right called Shuncheng, later called Xuanwu;
translations.idiomatic: to the south-right, Shuncheng, later Xuanwu;

sentences.zh: 東之南曰齊化，後曰朝陽；

translations.literal: east's south called Qihua, later called Chaoyang;
translations.idiomatic: on the east-south, Qihua, later Chaoyang;

translations.literal: east's north called Dongzhi;
translations.idiomatic: on the east-north, Dongzhi;

sentences.zh: 西之南曰平則，後曰阜成；

translations.literal: west's south called Pingze, later called Fucheng;
translations.idiomatic: on the west-south, Pingze, later Fucheng;

sentences.zh: 西之北曰彰儀，後曰西直；

translations.literal: west's north called Zhangyi, later called Xizhi;
translations.idiomatic: on the west-north, Zhangyi, later Xizhi;

translations.literal: north's east called Anding;
translations.idiomatic: on the north-east, Anding;

translations.literal: north's west called Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: on the north-west, Desheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年築重城，包京城之南，轉抱東西角樓，長二十八里。

translations.literal: Jiajing year thirty-two built outer wall, wrapping the capital city's south, turning to embrace east and west corner towers, length twenty-eight li.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 32 an outer wall was built around the southern sector of the capital, curving to join the eastern and western corner towers—twenty-eight li long.

sentences.zh: 門七：正南曰永定，南之左爲左安，南之右爲右安，東曰廣渠，東之北曰東便，西曰廣寧，西之北曰西便。

translations.literal: Gates seven: due south called Yongding; south's left was Zuo'an; south's right was You'an; east called Guangqu; east's north called Dongbian; west called Guangning; west's north called Xibian.
translations.idiomatic: It had seven gates: Yongding on the south; Zuo'an to the south-left; You'an to the south-right; Guangqu on the east; Dongbian on the east-north; Guangning on the west; Xibian on the west-north.

translations.literal: Governed departments five, counties twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: It governed five departments and twenty-two counties.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年編戶一十萬五百一十八，口六十六萬九千三十三。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year four registered households one hundred thousand five hundred eighteen, mouths six hundred sixty-nine thousand thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 4 it had 100,518 registered households and 669,033 persons.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年，戶一十萬一千一百三十四，口七十萬六千八百六十一。

translations.literal: Wanli year six, households one hundred thousand one hundred thirty-four, mouths seven hundred six thousand eight hundred sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 6 there were 100,134 households and 706,861 persons.

translations.literal: Daxing attached.
translations.idiomatic: Daxing (seat-attached county).

sentences.zh: 東南有大通河，亦日通惠河，水自玉河出，繞都城東南，下流至高麗莊，入白河，即元運河也。

translations.literal: Southeast has Great Canal River, also day Tonghui River; water from Jade River out, winds capital southeast, downstream to Gaoli village, enters White River—that is Yuan transport canal.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast runs the Grand Canal, also called the Tonghui River. Its water issues from the Jade River, skirts the capital's southeast, flows to Gaolizhuang, and joins the Bai River—the Yuan-era transport canal.

sentences.zh: 又有玉河，源自玉泉山，流經大內，出都城東南，注大通河。

translations.literal: Also there is Jade River, source from Jade Spring Mountain, flows through the inner palace, exits capital southeast, pours into Great Canal River.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade River rises at Jade Spring Mountain, passes through the inner palace, leaves the capital's southeast, and empties into the Grand Canal.

translations.literal: Wanping attached.
translations.idiomatic: Wanping (seat-attached county).

translations.literal: Western mountains in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Hills lie to the west.

sentences.zh: 有桑乾河出山西馬邑縣，流千里入京師宛平縣境。

translations.literal: There is Sanggan River exiting Shanxi Mayi county, flows a thousand li entering capital Wanping county territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Sanggan River rises in Mayi county, Shanxi, flows a thousand li, and enters Wanping county within the capital region.

sentences.zh: 出盧溝橋下，又東南分爲二：一至通州，入白河；

translations.literal: Exits below Lugou Bridge, again southeast divides into two: one reaching Tongzhou, enters White River;
translations.idiomatic: It passes beneath Lugou Bridge and splits southeast into two branches: one runs to Tongzhou and joins the Bai River;

sentences.zh: 一至武清小直沽，合衛河，入於海。

translations.literal: one reaching Wuqing Xiao Zhigou, joins Guard River, enters into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: the other runs to Xiaozhigou in Wuqing, joins the Wei River, and reaches the sea.

sentences.zh: 又有沙河、高梁河、清河，皆在西北。

translations.literal: Also there are Sha River, Gaoliang River, and Qing River—all in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: The northwest also has the Sha, Gaoliang, and Qing rivers.

sentences.zh: 西又有沿河口守禦千戶所，有盧溝、王平口、石港口、齊家莊四巡檢司。

translations.literal: West also has Yanhekou defensive thousand-household post; there are four patrol inspectorates: Lugou, Wangpingkou, Shigangkou, and Qijiazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: To the west stands the Yanhekou defensive thousand-household post, with patrol inspectorates at Lugou, Wangpingkou, Shigangkou, and Qijiazhuang.

translations.literal: Liangxiang, southwest of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liangxiang county lies southwest of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有琉璃河，即古聖水，下流入澱。

translations.literal: There is Liuli River, that is ancient Shengshui; downstream enters the marsh.
translations.idiomatic: The Liuli River—the ancient Shengshui—flows down into the marshlands.

translations.literal: North has Tianjin Pass.
translations.idiomatic: To the north is Tianjin Pass.

translations.literal: Gu'an, southwest of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gu'an county lies southwest of the prefecture.

translations.literal: Yuan Gu'an department.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it was Gu'an department.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年十二月降爲縣。

translations.literal: Hongwu year one, twelfth month, reduced to county.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Hongwu 1 it was reduced to a county.

translations.literal: Southwest has Juma River, that is Laishui.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest runs the Juma River, also called the Laishui.

sentences.zh: 源自代郡，下流合易水爲白溝，入三角澱。

translations.literal: Originates from Dai commandery; downstream joins Yi River as Baigou, enters Sanjiao Moor.
translations.idiomatic: It rises in Dai commandery, joins the Yi River downstream as the Baigou, and enters Sanjiao Moor.

translations.literal: Yongqing, south of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing county lies south of the prefecture.

translations.literal: South has Juma River.
translations.idiomatic: To the south is the Juma River.

translations.literal: Dong'an, southeast of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'an county lies southeast of the prefecture.

translations.literal: Yuan Dong'an department; administration was in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it was Dong'an department, with its seat in the west.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年十二月降爲縣。

translations.literal: Hongwu year one, twelfth month, reduced to county.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Hongwu 1 it was reduced to a county.

translations.literal: Year three moved to present seat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the seat was moved to its present site.

sentences.zh: 南有鳳河，即桑乾分流，南入三角澱。

translations.literal: South has Feng River, that is Sanggan branch stream; south enters Sanjiao Moor.
translations.idiomatic: To the south is the Feng River, a branch of the Sanggan, which flows south into Sanjiao Moor.

translations.literal: Xianghe, southeast of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghe county lies southeast of the prefecture.

translations.literal: Yuan belonged to Hu department.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it belonged to Hu department.

translations.literal: Hongwu year ten, second month, absorbed into the department.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Hongwu 10 it was absorbed into the department.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月復置，改屬府。

translations.literal: Year thirteen, second month, restored; changed to belong to prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 13 it was restored and placed under the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 西有板罾口河，源出通州東之孤山，經縣界，入於白河。

translations.literal: West has Bazengkou River; source from Gu Mountain east of Tongzhou; passes county border; enters Bai River.
translations.idiomatic: To the west is the Bazengkou River, rising at Gu Mountain east of Tongzhou, crossing the county, and joining the Bai River.

sentences.zh: 通州 洪武初，以州治潞縣省入。

translations.literal: Tongzhou. Early Hongwu, by absorbing Lu county at the department seat.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou Department: in early Hongwu the seat-administered Lu county was absorbed.

sentences.zh: 西有通惠河，西南有渾河，即桑乾，至州東張家灣，俱合於白河。

translations.literal: West has Tonghui River; southwest has Hun River, that is Sanggan; reaching Zhangjiawan east of the department, all join Bai River.
translations.idiomatic: To the west is the Tonghui River; to the southwest the Hun River—the Sanggan—which, with the Tonghui, meets the Bai River at Zhangjiawan east of the department.

translations.literal: There is Zhangjiawan patrol inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: It has a patrol inspectorate at Zhangjiawan.

translations.literal: Southwest has Hongren Bridge patrol inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest is the Hongren Bridge patrol inspectorate.

translations.literal: Forty li west from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It lies forty li west of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Governs four counties:
translations.idiomatic: It governed four counties:

translations.literal: Sanhe department, east.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe department, to the east.

translations.literal: North has Ju River.
translations.idiomatic: To the north is the Ju River.

sentences.zh: 又西有洳河，西南有鮑丘河，一名矣榆河，即東潞水，俱流入於泃河。

translations.literal: Also west has Ru River; southwest has Baoqiu River, one name Yi River, that is eastern Lu River—all flow into Ju River.
translations.idiomatic: To the west is the Ru River; to the southwest the Baoqiu, also called the Yi River—the eastern Lu River—all empty into the Ju.

sentences.zh: 西有泥窪鋪巡檢司，後移於夏店鋪。

translations.literal: West has Niwapu patrol inspectorate; later moved to Xiadianpu.
translations.idiomatic: To the west was the Niwapu patrol inspectorate, later moved to Xiadianpu.

translations.literal: Wuqing department, south.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqing department, to the south.

translations.literal: Yuan belonged to Hu department.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it belonged to Hu department.

translations.literal: Hongwu year twelve came under jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 12 it came under this jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 有三角澱，在縣南，即古之雍奴，週二百餘里，諸水所聚。

translations.literal: There is Sanjiao Moor, in the county south, that is ancient Yongnu; circuit two hundred-odd li, where all waters gather.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjiao Moor lies south of the county—the ancient Yongnu—some two hundred li in circuit, where the rivers converge.

sentences.zh: 有直沽，在縣東南，衛河、白河、丁字沽合流於此入海。

translations.literal: There is Zhigu, in the county southeast; Guard River, Bai River, and Dingzi Moor converge here to enter the sea.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhigu in the southeast, the Guard River, Bai River, and Dingzi Moor unite and reach the sea.

translations.literal: There is a patrol inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: There is a patrol inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 又東北有河西務、東南有楊村二巡檢司。

translations.literal: Also northeast has Hexiwu; southeast has Yangcun—two patrol inspectorates.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast is Hexiwu and to the southeast Yangcun—two patrol inspectorates.

translations.literal: Hu county department, south.
translations.idiomatic: Hu county department, to the south.

translations.literal: Yuan Hu department.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it was Hu department.

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年二月降爲縣來屬。

translations.literal: Hongwu year fourteen, second month, reduced to county and came under jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Hongwu 14 it was reduced to a county and placed under this jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 有漷河，一名新河，東入於白河，即盧溝之下流。

translations.literal: There is Hu River, one name Xin River; east enters Bai River—that is Lugou's lower reach.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu River, also called the Xin, flows east into the Bai—the lower course of the Lugou.

translations.literal: Baodi department, southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Baodi department, to the southeast.

translations.literal: Yuan directly attached Dadu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it was part of the directly attached Dadu circuit.

translations.literal: Hongwu year ten, second month, came under jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Hongwu 10 it came under this jurisdiction.

translations.literal: East has Chao River.
translations.idiomatic: To the east is the Chao River.

translations.literal: South has Ju River.
translations.idiomatic: To the south is the Ju River.

sentences.zh: 又縣東南有樑城守禦千戶所，建文二年，燕王置。

translations.literal: Also county southeast has Liangcheng defensive thousand-household post; Jianwen year two, Prince of Yan established.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the county is the Liangcheng defensive thousand-household post, established by the Prince of Yan in Jianwen 2.

translations.literal: There is Lutai patrol inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: There is a patrol inspectorate at Lutai.

sentences.zh: 霸州 洪武初，以州治益津縣省入。

translations.literal: Bazhou. Early Hongwu, by absorbing Yijin county at the department seat.
translations.idiomatic: Bazhou Department: in early Hongwu the seat-administered Yijin county was absorbed.

sentences.zh: 拒馬河舊在北，後徙治南。

translations.literal: Juma River formerly was in the north; later the seat moved south.
translations.idiomatic: The Juma River once lay to the north; later the seat was moved south of it.

translations.literal: Also south has Sha River.
translations.idiomatic: To the south is also the Sha River.

translations.literal: East has Yuanjiakou patrol inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: To the east is the Yuanjiakou patrol inspectorate.

translations.literal: Two hundred ten li north from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It lies 210 li north of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Governs three counties:
translations.idiomatic: It governed three counties:

translations.literal: Wen'an department, south slightly east.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an department, south-southeast of the seat.

translations.literal: West has Yi River.
translations.idiomatic: To the west is the Yi River.

translations.literal: Northeast has Desheng, Huoshao, and other moors.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast are Desheng, Huoshao, and other moors.

translations.literal: Dacheng department, southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng department, to the southeast.

sentences.zh: 東北有黃汊河，源自交河，分流至縣境，入三角澱。

translations.literal: Northeast has Huangcha River; source from Jiao River; branches to county territory; enters Sanjiao Moor.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast the Huangcha River branches from the Jiao River into the county and enters Sanjiao Moor.

translations.literal: Baoding department, south slightly west.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding department, south-southwest of the seat.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年九月省入霸州。

translations.literal: Hongwu year seven, ninth month, absorbed into Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Hongwu 7 it was absorbed into Bazhou.

translations.literal: Year thirteen, eleventh month, restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 13 it was restored.

sentences.zh: 玉帶河在北，東流入會通河。

translations.literal: Jade Belt River in the north; east flows into Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Belt River lies to the north and flows east into the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 西南有磁河，東南與玉帶河合。

translations.literal: Southwest has Ci River; southeast joins Jade Belt River.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest is the Ci River, which meets the Jade Belt River in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 涿州 洪武初以州治范陽縣省入。

translations.literal: Zhuozhou. Early Hongwu, by absorbing Fanyang county at the department seat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuozhou Department: in early Hongwu the seat-administered Fanyang county was absorbed.

translations.literal: West has Dulu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the west is Dulu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 北有涿水，西北有挾河，合焉。

translations.literal: North has Zhuo River; northwest has Xia River—they join.
translations.idiomatic: To the north is the Zhuo River; from the northwest the Xia River joins it.

translations.literal: South has Fan River.
translations.idiomatic: To the south is the Fan River.

translations.literal: One hundred forty li northeast from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It lies 140 li northeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Governs one county.
translations.idiomatic: It governed one county.

translations.literal: Fangshan department, north, slightly west.
translations.idiomatic: Fangshan department, north-northwest of the seat.

translations.literal: West has Great Fang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the west is Great Fang Mountain.

translations.literal: North has Great An Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the north is Great An Mountain.

sentences.zh: 西南有青龍潭，其下流爲挾河，一名韓村河，至涿州與胡良河合。

translations.literal: Southwest has Qinglong Pool; its lower stream is Xia River, one name Hancun River—to Zhuozhou joins Hu River.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest lies Qinglong Pool; its outlet, the Xia or Hancun River, reaches Zhuozhou and joins the Huliang River.

translations.literal: North has Cijiawu patrol inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: To the north is the Cijiawu patrol inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 昌平州元昌平縣，直隸大都路。

translations.literal: Changping department: Yuan Changping county, directly attached Dadu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Changping Department: under the Yuan it was Changping county in the directly attached Dadu circuit.

sentences.zh: 正德元年七月升爲州，旋罷。

translations.literal: Zhengde year one, seventh month, promoted to department; soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhengde 1 it was promoted to a department, then soon abolished.

translations.literal: Year eight again promoted to department.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 it was again promoted to a department.

sentences.zh: 舊治白浮圖城，景泰元年築永安城於東，三年遷縣治焉。

translations.literal: Old seat White Floating Pagoda City; Jingtai year one built Yong'an City to the east; year three moved county seat there.
translations.idiomatic: The old seat was at White Floating Pagoda City; in Jingtai 1 Yong'an City was built to the east, and in year 3 the county seat was moved there.

sentences.zh: 北有天壽山，成祖以下陵寢鹹在。

translations.literal: North has Tianshou Mountain; imperial mausoleums from Chengzu downward are all there.
translations.idiomatic: To the north is Tianshou Mountain, where the imperial mausoleums from the Yongle emperor onward all stand.

translations.literal: Southeast has White Floating Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast is White Floating Mountain.

translations.literal: Southwest has Imperial Sojourn Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest is Imperial Sojourn Mountain.

sentences.zh: 又南有榆河，一名溫餘河，下流爲沙河，入於白河。

translations.literal: Also south has Yu River, one name Wanyu River; lower stream is Sha River, enters Bai River.
translations.idiomatic: To the south is the Yu or Wanyu River, which becomes the Sha River and joins the Bai.

sentences.zh: 又東南有鞏華城，嘉靖十九年築。

translations.literal: Also southeast has Gonghua City, Jiajing year nineteen built.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast is Gonghua City, built in Jiajing 19.

translations.literal: Northeast has Huanghua Town.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast is Huanghua Town.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，置渤海守禦千戶所於此，萬曆元年移於慕田峪，四年復故。

translations.literal: Mid-Hongzhi, established Bohai defensive thousand-household post here; Wanli year one moved to Mutianyu; year four restored former site.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongzhi period a Bohai defensive thousand-household post was placed here; in Wanli 1 it moved to Mutianyu, and in year 4 returned to this site.

sentences.zh: 西有鎮邊城，又有常峪城，俱正德十年五月築，各置守禦千戶所。

translations.literal: West has Zhenbian City; also has Changyu City—all Zhengde year ten fifth month built, each established defensive thousand-household post.
translations.idiomatic: To the west are Zhenbian City and Changyu City—both built in the fifth month of Zhengde 10, each with its own defensive thousand-household post.

sentences.zh: 又有白陽守禦千戶所，亦正德中置。

translations.literal: Also there is Baiyang defensive thousand-household post, also Zhengde period established.
translations.idiomatic: A Baiyang defensive thousand-household post was also established in the Zhengde period.

translations.literal: Northwest has Juyong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest is Juyong Pass.

translations.literal: Ninety li south from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It lies ninety li south of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Governs three counties:
translations.idiomatic: It governed three counties:

translations.literal: Shunyi department, east slightly south.
translations.idiomatic: Shunyi department, east-southeast of the seat.

translations.literal: Yuan Shun department.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it was Shun department.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年十二月改爲順義縣，屬府。

translations.literal: Hongwu year one, twelfth month, changed to Shunyi county, belonged to prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Hongwu 1 it became Shunyi county under the prefecture.

translations.literal: Zhengde year one, seventh month, came under jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhengde 1 it came under this department's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 東有白河，西南有榆河，又有潮河，俱流入焉。

translations.literal: East has Bai River; southwest has Yu River; also has Chao River—all flow into it.
translations.idiomatic: The Bai River lies to the east, the Yu to the southwest, and the Chao also flows in.

translations.literal: Huairou department, northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Huairou department, to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年十一月省入檀州。

translations.literal: Hongwu year one, eleventh month, absorbed into Tan department.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Hongwu 1 it was absorbed into Tan department.

sentences.zh: 十二月復分密雲、 昌平二縣地置，屬府。

translations.literal: Twelfth month again divided Miyun and Changping two counties' territory to establish, subordinate to the prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2 it was demoted to a county.

translations.idiomatic: To the southwest are Gucheng, Danyang, Shijiu, and other lakes.

sentences.zh: 東南有廣通鎮，俗曰東壩，有廣通鎮巡檢司。

translations.literal: Southeast has Guangtong town, vulgarly called Dongba, with a Guangtong town patrol inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast is Guangtong town, commonly called Dongba, with a Guangtong town patrol inspectorate.

translations.literal: Jiangpu, west of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangpu—west of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 本六合縣浦子口巡檢司，洪武九年六月改爲縣，析和、滁二州及江寧縣地益之。

translations.idiomatic: There is also a patrol inspectorate at Xijiang Mouth.

translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 6 it was renamed Neutral Prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 7 it became Fengyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年九月建中都城於舊城西，三年十二月始成。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Hongwu 2 the Central Capital city was built west of the old city; in the twelfth month of year 3 it was first completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Hongwu 2 the Central Capital was built west of the old city and completed in the twelfth month of year 3.

sentences.zh: 週五十里四百四十三步。

translations.literal: Circuit fifty li four hundred forty-three paces.
translations.idiomatic: Its circuit was fifty li and four hundred forty-three paces.

sentences.zh: 立門九：正南曰洪武，南之左曰南左甲第，右曰前右甲第，北之東曰北左甲第，西曰後右甲第，正東曰獨山，東之左曰長春，右曰朝陽，正西曰塗山。

translations.literal: Nine gates were set up: due south called Hongwu; south left called South Left First Rank Residence, right called Front Right First Rank Residence; north east called North Left First Rank Residence, west called Rear Right First Rank Residence; due east called Dushan; east left called Changchun, right called Chaoyang; due west called Tushan.
translations.idiomatic: Nine gates were opened: due south, Hongwu; to its left, South Left First Rank Residence, and to its right, Front Right First Rank Residence; northeast, North Left First Rank Residence, and northwest, Rear Right First Rank Residence; due east, Dushan; east left, Changchun, and east right, Chaoyang; due west, Tushan.

sentences.zh: 中爲皇城，周九里三十步，正南門曰午門，北曰玄城，東曰東華，西曰西華。

translations.literal: Within was the imperial city, circuit nine li thirty paces; due south gate called Meridian Gate, north called Profound City, east called East Glory, west called West Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Inside stood the imperial city, nine li and thirty paces around; its south gate was the Meridian Gate, the north gate Profound City, the east East Glory, and the west West Glory.

translations.literal: Governing five prefectures and thirteen counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed five subprefectures and thirteen counties.

translations.literal: Distance from Nanjing three hundred thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: It lay three hundred thirty li from Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年編戶七萬九千一百七，口四十二萬七千三百三。

translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 26 it had 79,107 registered households and 427,303 persons.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，戶九萬五千一十，口九十三萬一千一百八。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 4, households ninety-five thousand ten, mouths nine hundred thirty-one thousand one hundred eight.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 4 it had 95,010 registered households and 931,108 persons.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年，戶一十一萬一千七十，口一百二十萬二千三百四十九。

translations.literal: Wanli year 6, households one hundred eleven thousand seventy, mouths one million two hundred two thousand three hundred forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 6 it had 111,070 registered households and 1,202,349 persons.

translations.literal: Fengyang, the seat.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang—the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年八月析臨淮縣地置，爲府治。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Hongwu 7 territory was taken from Linhuai county to establish it as the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Hongwu 7 land was taken from Linhuai county to establish the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 十一年又割虹縣地益之。

translations.literal: In year 11 territory was again cut from Hong county and added.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 more land was taken from Hong county and added.

sentences.zh: 北濱淮，南有鏌鋣山，西濠水出焉。

translations.idiomatic: It borders the Huai to the north; Moyecha Mountain lies to the south, whence the western Hao River rises.

sentences.zh: 又西南有皇陵城，洪武二年置衛。

translations.literal: Also southwest has Imperial Mausoleum City; in Hongwu year 2 a guard was established.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest also is Imperial Mausoleum City, where a guard was established in Hongwu 2.

sentences.zh: 西北有長淮關，洪武六年置長淮衛於此。

sentences.zh: 東北有洪塘湖屯田守禦千戶所，洪武十一年置。

translations.idiomatic: Linhuai—northeast of Fengyang Prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it was called Zhongli, the seat of Haozhou.

translations.idiomatic: In year 7 it was placed under the prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: It borders the Huai to the north.

translations.literal: There are two Hao Rivers: the eastern source issues from Haotang Mountain, the western source from Moyecha Mountain; at the city's southwest they join and flow east into the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Two Hao Rivers meet here: the eastern rises at Haotang Mountain and the western at Moyecha Mountain; southwest of the city they unite and flow east into the Huai.

translations.literal: Huaiyuan, northwest of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyuan—northwest of Fengyang Prefecture.

translations.literal: Jing Mountain is southwest of the county.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Mountain lies southwest of the county.

translations.literal: Tu Mountain is southeast of the county.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Mountain lies southeast of the county.

sentences.zh: 淮水經兩山峽間，有北肥水入焉。

translations.idiomatic: The Huai runs through the gorge between the two mountains, and the North Fei River joins it.

sentences.zh: 又北有渦水亦入淮，謂之渦口。

translations.idiomatic: To the north the Wo River also enters the Huai at what is called the Wo Mouth.

translations.idiomatic: It has a patrol inspectorate at Luohe town.

translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan—south of Fengyang Prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: To the west is the Luo River.

translations.idiomatic: Wuhe—northeast of Fengyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十五年遷於澮河北，即今治也。

translations.idiomatic: It borders the Huai to the east.

translations.idiomatic: To the southeast is the Chong River; to the northwest the Hui and Tuo rivers; to the northeast the Tong River—all unite and enter the Huai at the Five Rivers Mouth.

sentences.zh: 又西有上店巡檢司，後廢。

translations.literal: Also west had the Shangdian patrol inspectorate, later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: To the west there was once a patrol inspectorate at Shangdian, later abolished.

translations.literal: Hong, northeast of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hong county—northeast of Fengyang Prefecture.

translations.literal: Under the Yuan it belonged to Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it belonged to Sizhou.

translations.idiomatic: The Dabie Mountains lie to the southwest.

translations.idiomatic: Mengcheng—north of Fengyang Prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: In the Taizu's Wu year it belonged to Linhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年二月還屬府，後以州治臨淮縣省入。

translations.idiomatic: To the southeast is Duliang Mountain.

translations.literal: Northeast has Turtle Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast is Turtle Mountain.

translations.idiomatic: To the west is Fushan.

translations.idiomatic: Tianchang—southeast of Sizhou.

translations.idiomatic: Ye Mountain lies south of the county.

sentences.zh: 西北有石樑河，下流爲五湖，接高郵州界。

translations.idiomatic: To the northeast is the Chengmeng township patrol inspectorate.

translations.idiomatic: Suzhou—under the Yuan it belonged to Guide Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the second month of Hongwu 4 it came under this jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Hongwu 4 it was reassigned here.

sentences.zh: 龍山在西南，北肥水出焉。

translations.literal: Long Mountain is in the southwest; the North Fei River issues from it.
translations.idiomatic: Long Mountain lies to the southwest, whence the North Fei River rises.

sentences.zh: 又北有睢河，自河南永城縣流入，下流至宿遷縣合淮，亦曰小河也。

sentences.zh: 南有汴河，亦自永城縣流入，又有澮河與渙水合。

translations.idiomatic: To the southeast is also the Tuo River.

translations.idiomatic: It lies two hundred thirty-three li southeast of Fengyang Prefecture.

translations.literal: Southwest has Qimei Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest is Qimei Mountain.

translations.literal: North has Qingshi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the north is Qingshi Mountain.

translations.literal: Yellow River is in northeast.

translations.literal: South has Bian River.
translations.idiomatic: To the south is the Bian River.

translations.idiomatic: To the north is the Sui River.

sentences.zh: 又南有汝水，自河南息縣流入，經硃皋鎮入淮。
